Dataset context:
Mouse Organogenesis Spatiotemporal Transcriptomic Atlas (MOSTA) Stereo-seq at embryonic day 9.5, an early-organogenesis stage. The E9.5 files are sagittal sections from C57BL/6 mouse embryos; names such as E9.5_E1S1 identify the developmental stage, embryo/biological replicate, and section. The standard MOSTA section files are processed bin-50 expression matrices, so each observation aggregates a local spatial area rather than representing a guaranteed single cell. This profile summarizes one multi-observation expression-spatial prototype. The local E9.5_E1S1 reference contains 5,913 bins and 25,568 genes. Its annotation metadata describes 12 anatomical tissue domains: AGM, Brain, Branchial arch, Cavity, Connective tissue, Dermomyotome, Heart, Liver, Mesenchyme, Neural crest, Notochord, and Sclerotome. These names provide developmental context and evaluation metadata, not labels to predict.
The semantic evidence vector will be used by downstream multi-view learning: semantic-view graph construction, semantic pruning, and structure-semantic dual-confidence contrastive learning.

Task objective:
Extract ten continuous developmental-program evidence axes for unsupervised structure discovery in MOSTA E9.5 mouse-embryo Stereo-seq, not a hard organ, tissue-domain, or cell-type label. The evidence should preserve early organogenesis lineage relationships, distinguish coherent tissue programs from mixed bin-50 boundaries, improve semantic neighborhoods, and select reliable contrastive anchors without using annotation labels as input.

Evidence axes to score:
- brain_neuroectoderm
- neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme
- somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome
- notochord_axial_mesoderm
- cardiac_muscle_heart
- vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity
- hepatic_endoderm_liver
- boundary_or_mixed
- ambiguity
- confidence

Interpretation rules:
- Do not output any of the 12 annotation names as a hard domain label and do not infer a domain from spatial position alone.
- Treat the annotations as tissue domains that can contain multiple cell states; score only marker-supported developmental programs from the supplied genes and neighbor-prototype evidence.
- Use brain_neuroectoderm for coherent neural-tube or early-brain progenitor programs, not for every prototype with generic developmental genes.
- Use neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme for migratory neural-crest, pharyngeal/branchial-arch, mesenchymal, or extracellular-matrix-rich connective programs; preserve uncertainty when their origins cannot be separated.
- Use somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome for paraxial-mesoderm and somite-compartment programs, including dermomyotome/myogenic or sclerotome/chondrogenic evidence, without forcing a compartment assignment.
- Use notochord_axial_mesoderm only for coherent axial midline or notochord signaling evidence; shared neural developmental genes alone are insufficient.
- Keep cardiac contractile evidence separate from vascular/hematopoietic evidence: cardiac_muscle_heart reflects cardiomyocyte and heart-muscle programs, whereas vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity reflects endothelial, aortic/AGM, erythroid, or blood-rich cavity programs.
- Use hepatic_endoderm_liver for coherent early hepatic or endodermal programs; do not call liver from generic epithelial or proliferation signals alone.
- Because bin-50 observations and prototypes can span adjacent embryonic structures, conflicting lineage programs, transition zones, blood-filled cavities, or marker-sparse profiles should increase boundary_or_mixed and ambiguity.
- High confidence requires a coherent developmental program supported by both enriched markers and neighborhood context; stage expectations are context, not evidence by themselves.

Dataset context:
Mouse Organogenesis Spatiotemporal Transcriptomic Atlas (MOSTA) Stereo-seq at embryonic day 9.5, an early-organogenesis stage. The E9.5 files are sagittal sections from C57BL/6 mouse embryos; names such as E9.5_E1S1 identify the developmental stage, embryo/biological replicate, and section. The standard MOSTA section files are processed bin-50 expression matrices, so each observation aggregates a local spatial area rather than representing a guaranteed single cell. This profile summarizes one multi-observation expression-spatial prototype. The local E9.5_E1S1 reference contains 5,913 bins and 25,568 genes. Its annotation metadata describes 12 anatomical tissue domains: AGM, Brain, Branchial arch, Cavity, Connective tissue, Dermomyotome, Heart, Liver, Mesenchyme, Neural crest, Notochord, and Sclerotome. These names provide developmental context and evaluation metadata, not labels to predict.
The semantic evidence vector will be used by downstream multi-view learning: semantic-view graph construction, semantic pruning, and structure-semantic dual-confidence contrastive learning.

Task objective:
Extract ten continuous developmental-program evidence axes for unsupervised structure discovery in MOSTA E9.5 mouse-embryo Stereo-seq, not a hard organ, tissue-domain, or cell-type label. The evidence should preserve early organogenesis lineage relationships, distinguish coherent tissue programs from mixed bin-50 boundaries, improve semantic neighborhoods, and select reliable contrastive anchors without using annotation labels as input.

Evidence axes to score:
- brain_neuroectoderm
- neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme
- somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome
- notochord_axial_mesoderm
- cardiac_muscle_heart
- vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity
- hepatic_endoderm_liver
- boundary_or_mixed
- ambiguity
- confidence

Interpretation rules:
- Do not output any of the 12 annotation names as a hard domain label and do not infer a domain from spatial position alone.
- Treat the annotations as tissue domains that can contain multiple cell states; score only marker-supported developmental programs from the supplied genes and neighbor-prototype evidence.
- Use brain_neuroectoderm for coherent neural-tube or early-brain progenitor programs, not for every prototype with generic developmental genes.
- Use neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme for migratory neural-crest, pharyngeal/branchial-arch, mesenchymal, or extracellular-matrix-rich connective programs; preserve uncertainty when their origins cannot be separated.
- Use somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome for paraxial-mesoderm and somite-compartment programs, including dermomyotome/myogenic or sclerotome/chondrogenic evidence, without forcing a compartment assignment.
- Use notochord_axial_mesoderm only for coherent axial midline or notochord signaling evidence; shared neural developmental genes alone are insufficient.
- Keep cardiac contractile evidence separate from vascular/hematopoietic evidence: cardiac_muscle_heart reflects cardiomyocyte and heart-muscle programs, whereas vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity reflects endothelial, aortic/AGM, erythroid, or blood-rich cavity programs.
- Use hepatic_endoderm_liver for coherent early hepatic or endodermal programs; do not call liver from generic epithelial or proliferation signals alone.
- Because bin-50 observations and prototypes can span adjacent embryonic structures, conflicting lineage programs, transition zones, blood-filled cavities, or marker-sparse profiles should increase boundary_or_mixed and ambiguity.
- High confidence requires a coherent developmental program supported by both enriched markers and neighborhood context; stage expectations are context, not evidence by themselves.

The evidence should preserve early organogenesis lineage relationships, distinguish coherent tissue programs from mixed bin-50 boundaries, improve semantic neighborhoods, and select reliable contrastive anchors without using annotation labels as input.

Evidence axes to score:
- brain_neuroectoderm
- neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme
- somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome
- notochord_axial_mesoderm
- cardiac_muscle_heart
- vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity
- hepatic_endoderm_liver
- boundary_or_mixed
- ambiguity
- confidence

Interpretation rules:
- Do not output any of the 12 annotation names as a hard domain label and do not infer a domain from spatial position alone.
- Treat the annotations as tissue domains that can contain multiple cell states; score only marker-supported developmental programs from the supplied genes and neighbor-prototype evidence.
- Use brain_neuroectoderm for coherent neural-tube or early-brain progenitor programs, not for every prototype with generic developmental genes.
- Use neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme for migratory neural-crest, pharyngeal/branchial-arch, mesenchymal, or extracellular-matrix-rich connective programs; preserve uncertainty when their origins cannot be separated.
- Use somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome for paraxial-mesoderm and somite-compartment programs, including dermomyotome/myogenic or sclerotome/chondrogenic evidence, without forcing a compartment assignment.
- Use notochord_axial_mesoderm only for coherent axial midline or notochord signaling evidence; shared neural developmental genes alone are insufficient.
- Keep cardiac contractile evidence separate from vascular/hematopoietic evidence: cardiac_muscle_heart reflects cardiomyocyte and heart-muscle programs, whereas vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity reflects endothelial, aortic/AGM, erythroid, or blood-rich cavity programs.
- Use hepatic_endoderm_liver for coherent early hepatic or endodermal programs; do not call liver from generic epithelial or proliferation signals alone.
- Because bin-50 observations and prototypes can span adjacent embryonic structures, conflicting lineage programs, transition zones, blood-filled cavities, or marker-sparse profiles should increase boundary_or_mixed and ambiguity.
- High confidence requires a coherent developmental program supported by both enriched markers and neighborhood context; stage expectations are context, not evidence by themselves.

The E9.5 files are sagittal sections from C57BL/6 mouse embryos; names such as E9.5_E1S1 identify the developmental stage, embryo/biological replicate, and section. The standard MOSTA section files are processed bin-50 expression matrices, so each observation aggregates a local spatial area rather than representing a guaranteed single cell. This profile summarizes one multi-observation expression-spatial prototype. The local E9.5_E1S1 reference contains 5,913 bins and 25,568 genes. Its annotation metadata describes 12 anatomical tissue domains: AGM, Brain, Branchial arch, Cavity, Connective tissue, Dermomyotome, Heart, Liver, Mesenchyme, Neural crest, Notochord, and Sclerotome. These names provide developmental context and evaluation metadata, not labels to predict.
The semantic evidence vector will be used by downstream multi-view learning: semantic-view graph construction, semantic pruning, and structure-semantic dual-confidence contrastive learning.

Task objective:
Extract ten continuous developmental-program evidence axes for unsupervised structure discovery in MOSTA E9.5 mouse-embryo Stereo-seq, not a hard organ, tissue-domain, or cell-type label. The evidence should preserve early organogenesis lineage relationships, distinguish coherent tissue programs from mixed bin-50 boundaries, improve semantic neighborhoods, and select reliable contrastive anchors without using annotation labels as input.

Evidence axes to score:
- brain_neuroectoderm
- neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme
- somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome
- notochord_axial_mesoderm
- cardiac_muscle_heart
- vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity
- hepatic_endoderm_liver
- boundary_or_mixed
- ambiguity
- confidence

Interpretation rules:
- Do not output any of the 12 annotation names as a hard domain label and do not infer a domain from spatial position alone.
- Treat the annotations as tissue domains that can contain multiple cell states; score only marker-supported developmental programs from the supplied genes and neighbor-prototype evidence.
- Use brain_neuroectoderm for coherent neural-tube or early-brain progenitor programs, not for every prototype with generic developmental genes.
- Use neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme for migratory neural-crest, pharyngeal/branchial-arch, mesenchymal, or extracellular-matrix-rich connective programs; preserve uncertainty when their origins cannot be separated.
- Use somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome for paraxial-mesoderm and somite-compartment programs, including dermomyotome/myogenic or sclerotome/chondrogenic evidence, without forcing a compartment assignment.
- Use notochord_axial_mesoderm only for coherent axial midline or notochord signaling evidence; shared neural developmental genes alone are insufficient.
- Keep cardiac contractile evidence separate from vascular/hematopoietic evidence: cardiac_muscle_heart reflects cardiomyocyte and heart-muscle programs, whereas vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity reflects endothelial, aortic/AGM, erythroid, or blood-rich cavity programs.
- Use hepatic_endoderm_liver for coherent early hepatic or endodermal programs; do not call liver from generic epithelial or proliferation signals alone.
- Because bin-50 observations and prototypes can span adjacent embryonic structures, conflicting lineage programs, transition zones, blood-filled cavities, or marker-sparse profiles should increase boundary_or_mixed and ambiguity.
- High confidence requires a coherent developmental program supported by both enriched markers and neighborhood context; stage expectations are context, not evidence by themselves.

Dataset context:
Mouse Organogenesis Spatiotemporal Transcriptomic Atlas (MOSTA) Stereo-seq at embryonic day 9.5, an early-organogenesis stage. The E9.5 files are sagittal sections from C57BL/6 mouse embryos; names such as E9.5_E1S1 identify the developmental stage, embryo/biological replicate, and section. The standard MOSTA section files are processed bin-50 expression matrices, so each observation aggregates a local spatial area rather than representing a guaranteed single cell. This profile summarizes one multi-observation expression-spatial prototype. The local E9.5_E1S1 reference contains 5,913 bins and 25,568 genes. Its annotation metadata describes 12 anatomical tissue domains: AGM, Brain, Branchial arch, Cavity, Connective tissue, Dermomyotome, Heart, Liver, Mesenchyme, Neural crest, Notochord, and Sclerotome. These names provide developmental context and evaluation metadata, not labels to predict.
The semantic evidence vector will be used by downstream multi-view learning: semantic-view graph construction, semantic pruning, and structure-semantic dual-confidence contrastive learning.

Task objective:
Extract ten continuous developmental-program evidence axes for unsupervised structure discovery in MOSTA E9.5 mouse-embryo Stereo-seq, not a hard organ, tissue-domain, or cell-type label. The evidence should preserve early organogenesis lineage relationships, distinguish coherent tissue programs from mixed bin-50 boundaries, improve semantic neighborhoods, and select reliable contrastive anchors without using annotation labels as input.

Evidence axes to score:
- brain_neuroectoderm
- neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme
- somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome
- notochord_axial_mesoderm
- cardiac_muscle_heart
- vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity
- hepatic_endoderm_liver
- boundary_or_mixed
- ambiguity
- confidence

Interpretation rules:
- Do not output any of the 12 annotation names as a hard domain label and do not infer a domain from spatial position alone.
- Treat the annotations as tissue domains that can contain multiple cell states; score only marker-supported developmental programs from the supplied genes and neighbor-prototype evidence.
- Use brain_neuroectoderm for coherent neural-tube or early-brain progenitor programs, not for every prototype with generic developmental genes.
- Use neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme for migratory neural-crest, pharyngeal/branchial-arch, mesenchymal, or extracellular-matrix-rich connective programs; preserve uncertainty when their origins cannot be separated.
- Use somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome for paraxial-mesoderm and somite-compartment programs, including dermomyotome/myogenic or sclerotome/chondrogenic evidence, without forcing a compartment assignment.
- Use notochord_axial_mesoderm only for coherent axial midline or notochord signaling evidence; shared neural developmental genes alone are insufficient.
- Keep cardiac contractile evidence separate from vascular/hematopoietic evidence: cardiac_muscle_heart reflects cardiomyocyte and heart-muscle programs, whereas vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity reflects endothelial, aortic/AGM, erythroid, or blood-rich cavity programs.

- Because bin-50 observations and prototypes can span adjacent embryonic structures, conflicting lineage programs, transition zones, blood-filled cavities, or marker-sparse profiles should increase boundary_or_mixed and ambiguity.
- High confidence requires a coherent developmental program supported by both enriched markers and neighborhood context; stage expectations are context, not evidence by themselves.

The E9.5 files are sagittal sections from C57BL/6 mouse embryos; names such as E9.5_E1S1 identify the developmental stage, embryo/biological replicate, and section. The standard MOSTA section files are processed bin-50 expression matrices, so each observation aggregates a local spatial area rather than representing a guaranteed single cell. This profile summarizes one multi-observation expression-spatial prototype. The local E9.5_E1S1 reference contains 5,913 bins and 25,568 genes. Its annotation metadata describes 12 anatomical tissue domains: AGM, Brain, Branchial arch, Cavity, Connective tissue, Dermomyotome, Heart, Liver, Mesenchyme, Neural crest, Notochord, and Sclerotome. These names provide developmental context and evaluation metadata, not labels to predict.
The semantic evidence vector will be used by downstream multi-view learning: semantic-view graph construction, semantic pruning, and structure-semantic dual-confidence contrastive learning.

Task objective:
Extract ten continuous developmental-program evidence axes for unsupervised structure discovery in MOSTA E9.5 mouse-embryo Stereo-seq, not a hard organ, tissue-domain, or cell-type label. The evidence should preserve early organogenesis lineage relationships, distinguish coherent tissue programs from mixed bin-50 boundaries, improve semantic neighborhoods, and select reliable contrastive anchors without using annotation labels as input.

Evidence axes to score:
- brain_neuroectoderm
- neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme
- somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome
- notochord_axial_mesoderm
- cardiac_muscle_heart
- vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity
- hepatic_endoderm_liver
- boundary_or_mixed
- ambiguity
- confidence

Interpretation rules:
- Do not output any of the 12 annotation names as a hard domain label and do not infer a domain from spatial position alone.
- Treat the annotations as tissue domains that can contain multiple cell states; score only marker-supported developmental programs from the supplied genes and neighbor-prototype evidence.
- Use brain_neuroectoderm for coherent neural-tube or early-brain progenitor programs, not for every prototype with generic developmental genes.
- Use neural_crest_branchial_mesenchyme for migratory neural-crest, pharyngeal/branchial-arch, mesenchymal, or extracellular-matrix-rich connective programs; preserve uncertainty when their origins cannot be separated.
- Use somitic_dermomyotome_sclerotome for paraxial-mesoderm and somite-compartment programs, including dermomyotome/myogenic or sclerotome/chondrogenic evidence, without forcing a compartment assignment.
- Use notochord_axial_mesoderm only for coherent axial midline or notochord signaling evidence; shared neural developmental genes alone are insufficient.
- Keep cardiac contractile evidence separate from vascular/hematopoietic evidence: cardiac_muscle_heart reflects cardiomyocyte and heart-muscle programs, whereas vascular_hematopoietic_agm_cavity reflects endothelial, aortic/AGM, erythroid, or blood-rich cavity programs.
- Use hepatic_endoderm_liver for coherent early hepatic or endodermal programs; do not call liver from generic epithelial or proliferation signals alone.
- Because bin-50 observations and prototypes can span adjacent embryonic structures, conflicting lineage programs, transition zones, blood-filled cavities, or marker-sparse profiles should increase boundary_or_mixed and ambiguity.
- High confidence requires a coherent developmental program supported by both enriched markers and neighborhood context; stage expectations are context, not evidence by themselves.
